title: Weight-Space Programming of Variational Quantum Circuits: Large Language Models Write Quantum Circuit Parameters Without an Optimizer
read_level: full (arXiv HTML v1 main text Secs 1-8 and Reproducibility; Appendix B tables not read; figures as captions only)
metadata_mismatch: Author name: metadata 'Vasant G Honavar', paper 'Vasant Honavar'. Metadata abstract wording differs from the HTML v1 abstract (metadata begins 'Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) optimize circuit angles...', HTML begins 'Variational quantum algorithms train the angles...'); same substance.
why_wsp: GPT-6 Astra writes the gate angles (and in one setting the circuit itself) of variational quantum circuits directly from a problem description, with no loss, gradient or accuracy feedback.
facets: application domain: quantum computing (VQE, QAOA, QML)
domain: Variational quantum algorithms: VQE (TFIM, Heisenberg, H2), QAOA MaxCut, quantum digit classification
editor: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI Responses API, default reasoning, 32,000-token output budget)
target: Parameterized quantum circuits, <=8 qubits, 1-54 angles (e.g. HVA 4/8 angles, HEA 18/30 angles, fixed-ansatz QML 12-54 weights, QAOA 2p angles)
interface: direct values (JSON list of angles; or circuit in a small JSON circuit language)
loop: one-shot (only syntactic validation feedback, at most two retries; never used)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: n/a (writes all angles from scratch); e.g. 'by setting 19–21 of the 30 angles to exactly zero' (Sec 5.1)

headline_results.quote: On every one the model's angles are within 0.007 of the optimizer on the [0,1] spectrum scale, and on seven of eleven they are within 0.001

headline_results.claim: H2 exact ground state via closed form
headline_results.quote: returns its minimizer θ*=-arctan(0.1820/0.7782)=-0.2297 , the exact ground state
At depth p=1 the model's angles are optimal on all six graphs
Over all 42 requests the mean ratio is 0.748 as written and 0.856 with the sign corrected, against 0.849 for the optimizer
L-BFGS-B reached the target in a median of one loss evaluation in both VQE and QAOA ... the means are 48 and 36 evaluations, against 607 and 263 from random starts
0.926 ± 0.033 and 0.963 ± 0.019 , above the optimizer trained on the same examples ( 0.867 )
On all ten classes with three examples each it scores 0.653 ± 0.053 (chance 0.1 ), against 0.17 for the optimizer on the same thirty images and 0.76 for logistic regression
the model stays at chance throughout ( 0.07 – 0.14 )

cost.quote: A request cost on average 1.8k output tokens and 45 s for QAOA, 3.0k tokens and 160 s for VQE, and 5.2–5.5k tokens and 100–150 s for QML
the ten-class free-design circuits were the largest replies (14k tokens, 240 s)

baselines_and_controls: Random angles (50 draws VQE/QAOA, 20 QML); L-BFGS-B with finite differences from random starts (5 restarts VQE/QAOA, 1 QML) on same examples; optimizer warm-started from model's angles; exact diagonalization / brute-force MaxCut; logistic regression on raw pixels; optimizer with 200 training images.
runs_and_variance: 139 requests; each prompt sent 3 times (VQE, QAOA, fixed-ansatz QML) or 5 times (free-design QML); mean ± s.d. over repeats. Quote: 'Each prompt is sent 3 times ... or 5 times ... the reported mean ± standard deviation is over these repeats.' (Sec 3)
robustness_of_edits: not tested (all circuits noise-free simulation; no hardware)
verification: Exact state-vector simulation cross-checked against Qiskit; no formal verification
memorization_vs_reasoning: Replies show analytic derivations (H2 energy formula, QAOA p=1 expectation). Authors state: 'the model has certainly seen the Ising model, QAOA on regular graphs and the digits data set during training; part of what we measure is recall.'
limitations_stated: <=8 qubits, noise-free simulation; well-known problems (recall); modest optimizer baseline; single model; no feedback setting; fails on opaque weight spaces; sign-convention errors.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 (weight-space programming, MIT CSAIL)
notes_for_survey: Extends WSP writing to quantum circuit parameters in a strict no-feedback setting. Reports success tied to interpretability of weights, with failure on deeper fixed ansatz (chance at 30-54 weights for 10 classes) and a systematic sign-convention error in 6/42 QAOA replies.
